pass_b_english: A certain widow named Chrestē was being distressed by a wild spirit, terribly cutting herself, though she was of noble birth.
She intended to travel toward the sunrise the following day; having heard about those who had been healed by Jesus, she resolved to go during that night.
The holy Longinus appeared to her, standing outside of his head.
When she asked, "Who has come here?" the holy Longinus said to her, "Do you wish to be healed?"

She replied, "Yes, Lord, this is my desire." The holy man said to her, "Go to Jerusalem, find the house of Lucius the governor, and seek the head of Longinus the centurion. Bring it to my body, and you shall be saved.
For I am Longinus, the one who tends the sheep by the roadside, and I have not found rest in the place where I was buried until now; but do this, and you shall be healed in the name of Jesus Christ.
Not only will you be healed, but I will also recruit your son, for I am the one speaking to you from outside of the head."

Upon hearing these things, the woman arranged and organized her affairs with her friends. She set out on the road, and having reached the monument, she cried out with a great voice, saying, "Lord, who is in this place, just as you revealed to me in the vision, I am coming, so help me!"
Immediately the place was shaken, and a voice came to her, saying, "Go, for the Christ is the one helping you." Having heard this voice, she traveled her entire way in joy.
When she arrived in Jerusalem, she learned from the people of the city where the house of the governor was, where they were seeking the head of the holy Longinus.
And the governor gave her a sum of honor consisting of two hundred silver denarii.
Having received this, the woman prayed and glorified God for the completion, as though she were being made worthy of the grace of God.
After receiving the head of the honored Longinus along with her son Christos, she prepared to depart in the evening.
And behold, three angels appeared to her, whose glory she was unable to behold; they held white candles in their hands and went before her, singing a hymn to God throughout the entire night.
When the dawn was breaking, they rested in the place where they had arrived to take their food.

After three days, she brought the head of the honored Longinus to his village, having traveled there with her son Christos, and she sent it to the place where he was lying at the sixth hour of the night.
